Tomato.seed_identification: Small, flat, pale fuzzy beige, 3-4 mm.
Tomato.planting: Sow 1/4 inch deep, space 24-36 inches apart.

Potato.seed_identification: Grown from seed potatoes (tubers with eyes).
Potato.watering: Keep evenly moist, avoid soggy soil.

Cotton.seed_identification: Fuzzy, dark brown to black ovate seeds.
Cotton.planting: Sow 1-2 inches deep after final frost.

Mango.seed_identification: Large, flat, oblong pit with a woody husk.
Mango.planting: Plant grafted saplings in wide holes.

Apple.planting: Plant grafted bare-root trees in spring.

Corn.planting: Sow 1.5-2 inches deep in blocks for pollination.
Corn.watering: 1.5 inches per week, crucial during tasseling.

Soybean.seed_identification: Round, pale yellow to green beans.

Strawberry.seed_identification: Tiny, yellowish seeds on fruit exterior.
Strawberry.planting: Plant crowns at soil level, 18 inches apart.

Grape.planting: Plant dormant vines in deep holes.
Grape.watering: Moderate, avoid overhead watering to prevent rot.

Blueberry.watering: Keep roots constantly moist but not waterlogged.

Cherry.planting: Plant in well-draining soil to avoid root rot.

Pepper.watering: Even moisture, let soil dry slightly between waterings.

Orange.planting: Plant grafted saplings in sandy loam.

Lemon.planting: Plant in well-draining soil, protect from frost.
Lemon.watering: Allow top 2 inches to dry between watering.

Lime.seed_identification: Small, white to pale green seeds.
Lime.planting: Plant in well-draining, slightly acidic soil.

Banana.seed_identification: Commercial varieties are seedless (grown from pups).

Rice.seed_identification: Oblong grains encased in a rough hull.
Rice.planting: Broadcast seeds in flooded paddies or drill in dry fields.
Rice.watering: Requires flooded or consistently saturated soil.

Barley.seed_identification: Elliptical grains with a distinct crease.

Oats.planting: Sow 1 inch deep in early spring.

Rye.planting: Sow 1 inch deep; excellent cover crop.

Sorghum.seed_identification: Small, round, reddish-brown to white seeds.
Sorghum.planting: Sow 1 inch deep when soil warms.
Sorghum.watering: Highly drought tolerant; water during flowering.

Peanut.seed_identification: Ovate nuts enclosed in a fibrous shell.
Peanut.planting: Sow seeds 1.5-2 inches deep in loose, sandy soil.
Peanut.watering: Moderate; soil must remain loose for pegging.

Sunflower.watering: Deep watering to encourage deep roots.

Canola.planting: Sow 1/2 inch deep in cool weather.

Coffee.seed_identification: Greenish, grooved beans (seeds inside the cherry).
Coffee.planting: Start in nurseries, transplant at 12-18 months.

Tea.planting: Often grown from cuttings to maintain genetics.

Onion.planting: Sow 1/4 inch deep or plant sets.

Garlic.planting: Plant cloves 2 inches deep, pointy end up in fall.

Carrot.planting: Sow directly 1/4 inch deep in loose, rock-free soil.
Carrot.watering: Keep surface constantly moist until germination.

Radish.planting: Sow 1/2 inch deep, thin to 2 inches apart.
Radish.watering: Consistent moisture to prevent woody texture.

Cabbage.planting: Sow 1/4 inch deep, space 12-24 inches apart.
Cabbage.watering: Heavy watering to form tight heads.

Cauliflower.watering: Consistent moisture; highly sensitive to drought.

Spinach.planting: Sow 1/2 inch deep in cool weather.

Lettuce.planting: Sow 1/8 inch deep (requires light to germinate).

Cucumber.planting: Sow 1 inch deep in mounds or on trellises.
Cucumber.watering: High water needs; keep leaves dry.

Watermelon.seed_identification: Flat, teardrop-shaped, black or white seeds.
Watermelon.planting: Sow 1 inch deep in warm mounds.
Watermelon.watering: Heavy watering until fruit sets, then reduce.

Pumpkin.planting: Sow 1-2 inches deep in large mounds.

Pea.seed_identification: Round, wrinkled or smooth green/yellow spheres.
Pea.planting: Sow 1-2 inches deep in cool weather.

Lentil.planting: Sow 1 inch deep in early spring.

Chickpea.watering: Low to moderate; highly drought tolerant.

Almond.seed_identification: Teardrop-shaped kernel inside a hard shell.
Almond.planting: Plant bare-root trees in well-draining soil.
Almond.watering: Deep watering, especially during nut fill.

Walnut.seed_identification: Brain-shaped kernel inside a hard, round shell.

Pecan.watering: Requires large amounts of water in late summer.

Pistachio.seed_identification: Greenish kernel inside a split beige shell.
Pistachio.planting: Requires both male and female trees.
Pistachio.watering: Highly drought tolerant but yields better with water.

Cashew.seed_identification: Kidney-shaped seed attached to the bottom of the cashew apple.
Cashew.planting: Plant seeds or grafted saplings in sandy soil.
Cashew.watering: Drought tolerant; requires distinct dry season.

Coconut.seed_identification: Massive, fibrous drupe (the entire coconut is the seed).
Coconut.planting: Bury nut halfway in sandy soil.

Date.planting: Typically grown from offshoots to guarantee gender.
Date.watering: Roots need water, but crown needs extreme dry heat.

Fig.seed_identification: Tiny, crunchy seeds inside the syconium (fruit).

Pomegranate.seed_identification: Ruby-red arils containing a small hard seed.
Pomegranate.watering: Drought tolerant, but regular watering increases fruit size.

Nectarine.seed_identification: Deeply pitted, woody pit (identical to peach).

Kiwi.seed_identification: Tiny, black seeds scattered in flesh.
Kiwi.planting: Requires sturdy trellis; plant male and female vines.

Papaya.planting: Sow directly in warm, well-draining soil.
Papaya.watering: Moderate; highly susceptible to root rot.

Pineapple.seed_identification: Typically seedless; grown from crowns or slips.
Pineapple.planting: Plant the leafy crown in well-draining soil.
Pineapple.watering: Low water requirements; absorbs through leaves.

Avocado.planting: Plant grafted saplings in mounds for drainage.

Guava.watering: Drought tolerant but thrives with deep watering.

Olive.planting: Plant in highly draining, rocky soil.

Vanilla.seed_identification: Microscopic black seeds inside the pod.

Black Pepper.planting: Grown from cuttings on support trees.

Cinnamon.planting: Propagated via cuttings for bark harvest.

Ginger.watering: Keep evenly moist but not soggy.

Cardamom.seed_identification: Sticky, dark brown seeds inside green pods.

Coriander.seed_identification: Round, ridged, light brown seeds (cilantro seeds).

Mint.seed_identification: Dust-like seeds; usually grown from cuttings.
Mint.planting: Plant in containers to prevent invasive spreading.

Oregano.watering: Allow soil to dry completely between watering.

Rosemary.seed_identification: Small, brown seeds; best grown from cuttings.
Rosemary.watering: Allow to dry out completely between watering.

Parsley.planting: Soak seeds overnight, sow 1/4 inch deep.

Dill.planting: Sow directly; does not transplant well.

Lavender.planting: Plant in poor, highly draining soil.

Mustard.seed_identification: Tiny, round, reddish-brown to yellow seeds.

Sesame.planting: Sow 1/4 inch deep in warm soil.

Jute.watering: Requires standing water or extreme rainfall.

Yam.planting: Plant tuber pieces in large mounds.
Yam.watering: Requires consistent moisture during growth phase.

Sweet Potato.planting: Plant slips in warm, loose mounds.

Taro.planting: Plant corms deep in rich soil.
Taro.watering: Can be grown in flooded conditions or boggy soil.

Quinoa.seed_identification: Small, flat, round seeds with a bitter saponin coating.
Quinoa.planting: Sow 1/4 inch deep in cool weather.

Amaranth.seed_identification: Microscopic, shiny black or pale seeds.
Amaranth.planting: Surface sow or cover very lightly.
